tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). # Test suite rules

Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.

## The suites

- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.

## Building and running

Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.

- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`

Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".

## Where a test goes

- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.

## Use the existing helpers

Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.

- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.

## Writing the test

- Name the test case as a plain behavioral sentence in the present tense. No `Subsystem:` prefix.
- Tag it with the subsystem it covers, matching the file, in PascalCase. That tag is what people filter on, so every test needs one.
- Add further tags where they help: a narrower one to slice a large file (`[Rotcalip]`, `[Placer]`), a shared one for something spanning files (`[Python]`, `[H2C]`, `[Regression]`), or `[NotWorking]` / `[.]` to disable or hide a test. Say why in a comment if you disable or hide.
- Prefer a flat `TEST_CASE` per behavior, with `GENERATE` for parameterized cases. Reserve `SCENARIO` / `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` for genuine shared setup that branches into a few close variations.
- Set the config keys your test depends on, and derive the expected values from what you set. A 20mm cube sliced at `layer_height` 2 is 10 layers, and the test should state both parts. If a number in your assertion comes from a key you never set, the test is also testing that default.
- Assert the defining property, not an incidental value. "Skirt present" or "at least 2 brim loops" survives a refactor; exact coordinates and byte counts do not.
- Name a regression test for the behavior it protects, never for an issue or PR number.
- When asserting on G-code, match the meaningful token such as `; skirt` rather than whole lines, whitespace or comment wording. Depend on ordering only when ordering is the contract.

## Catch2 rules that cause real breakage

- Never reuse a `SECTION` name inside a loop. Use `DYNAMIC_SECTION` so each iteration is unique.
- Never assert from a spawned thread. Catch2 assertions are not thread-safe. Collect results in the thread and assert on the main thread.
- Never combine conditions with `&&` or `||` inside one assertion. Split them so Catch2 can print both operands on failure.
- Compare floats with `WithinAbs` or `WithinRel`, never `==`. Prefer these over `Approx` in new tests.
- Keep tests self-contained: no shared state, green under `--order rand`.

def pack_checkout(user, redirect_url: str) -> str:
    """The address of Chargebee's checkout for one credit pack."""
    result = chargebee.HostedPage.checkout_one_time_for_items({
        'customer': {'id': ensure_customer(user)},
        'item_prices': [{'item_price_id': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK_PRICE_ID, 'quantity': 1}],
        'redirect_url': redirect_url,
    }, env=_site())
    return result.hosted_page.url


def plan_checkout(user, plan_id: str, redirect_url: str) -> str:
    """The address of Chargebee's checkout for a plan: a new subscription, or a
    switch of the one the account has. An Obico Premium subscriber's carries
    the discount coupon. A coupon code, such as the one a JusPrin 1
    subscriber is emailed, goes in the checkout's own "Apply coupon" field."""
    current = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    live = current is not None and current.external_id and current.is_active and is_v2_plan(current.plan_id)
    payload = {'redirect_url': redirect_url}
    if obico_premium(user):
        payload['coupon_ids'] = [settings.JUSPRIN_V2_OBICO_COUPON]
    # A subscription has one plan, so the new plan replaces the current one.
    payload['subscription_items'] = [{'item_price_id': plan_id}]
    if live:
        payload['subscription'] = {'id': current.external_id}
        result = chargebee.HostedPage.checkout_existing_for_items(payload, env=_site())
    else:
        payload['customer'] = {'id': ensure_customer(user)}
        result = chargebee.HostedPage.checkout_new_for_items(payload, env=_site())
    return result.hosted_page.url

I made no new app commits; the branch still ends at 6c776dc2b5. One server change is uncommitted in tsd-enterprise: a Chargebee checkout the person cancelled goes back to the prices page instead of raising, with two new tests. All 310 server tests pass, and every check below was rerun after the last change.

**1. A picture whose file is gone.** I ran this as a probe in `agent_bridge_tests`, then removed it.
- The probe deleted the file behind an image attachment record. `state_request` then threw "could not open …/pic.jpg" and sent nothing.
- `hello` sent `hello_ack`, then threw before the project state went out. So the page counts as connected but never gets the chat history, the chat list or the project. `create_conversation` threw too.
- `user_message` still worked: the message was added and the reply came back. So the person can still send messages, but sees no history and cannot start or switch chats until the file comes back.
- I did not run the dialog count; this part is from reading the code. Each page message that throws sends its own report: one on load, then one for each new chat, chat switch or resync. With automatic reports off, each report opens a dialog.

**2. Tool calls with code `failed`.**
- **Producers:** the select, rename, duplicate, remove and plate actions, the printable switch, opening a gizmo, render and encode, writing G-code, 3MF, STL and preset files, cut, split, merge and repair, the printer setup that stops partway, generating calibration, and opening or importing a file.
- **Slicing is not among them.** When OrcaSlicer refuses a slice, `slice_start` still succeeds and carries the reason. A run that fails later is told in a new turn. The existing test "slice_start says whether OrcaSlicer began a run…" checks this.
- **A broken file the person picked is among them.** I ran a probe in the shell harness on a `.stl` that is not a mesh. Both `object_import_file` and `project_open` ended with `failed` ("The app did not import/open that file"), and no dialog was shown. A mesh that OrcaSlicer's repair cannot fix also ends `failed`. These reports are noise in Sentry.
- **Proposal, not built:** return `refused` in those three places (open, import, repair) and keep reporting `failed` as it is. The model's instruction is the same for both codes.
- **Side finding:** `pump_tools` has no guard against being re-entered. When the harness pumps directly, Orca's load progress dialog lets the shell timer run the same call a second time, and it throws "Tool call t-1 already ended". On macOS the timer cannot re-enter itself, so the real app should be safe there. Windows is unverified.

**3. Checkout.** Chargebee's docs say the return address is used only "upon successful checkout". A cancel goes to `cancel_url` with the page's id and state added. We pass no `cancel_url`, so the cancel address comes from the site's Hosted Pages settings, which I could not read. A cancelled checkout can therefore reach `checkout_done`, so `finish_checkout` now returns None for the cancelled state. Other states, and a checkout that belongs to another account, still raise.
- Before the fix, the new cancel test raised "came back cancelled"; after it, the cancel goes to prices.
- A second test confirms that coming back twice grants the pack once.
- A tab the person closes never redirects at all.
- Sources: [hosted pages](https://apidocs.chargebee.com/docs/api/hosted_pages), [create checkout for a new subscription](https://apidocs.chargebee.com/docs/api/hosted_pages/create-checkout-for-a-new-subscription).

# Error-handling sweep: trial findings

This file is the result of a reading-only sweep. It checks JusPrin's AI chat and Home code, and the JusPrin Cloud server's v2 code, against the trial copy of the error-handling rules and the `error-handling` audit skill. Nothing was built, run, changed or committed.

What was read:
- **Desktop app:** every `.cpp`/`.hpp` under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` and `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/` at commit `5e173c5e15`.
- **Server:** every `.py` under `web_ent/jusprin/v2/` except `tests/` and `migrations/`, at `2086b2ec64` in tsd-enterprise.

How it was judged:
- An outcome counts as decided by a person only if its cause is in `expected-errors-app.cpp` or `expected-errors-server.py`.
- Every other outcome counts as an unexpected error.

How to read the locations:
- Line numbers are from those two commits.
- App paths start at `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Server paths start at `web_ent/jusprin/v2/`.
- "Confirmed" means I read the code myself. Several findings were first reported by a reader subagent and then confirmed by me.
- Nothing was confirmed by running code.

## 1. Findings, most harmful first

### 1. In the desktop app, no failure is ever reported, and a thrown one reaches OrcaSlicer's generic handler
- **Where:**
  - The entry-point handler is `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:926-947` (`on_page_message`). It catches `json::exception`, adds the message type and id, and rethrows. That part is allowed.
  - The rethrow, and every other throw from the chat page, the timer pumps, Home's page messages (`Home/HomeHost.cpp:161`), Home's `CallAfter` bodies (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:749`, `:769-785`, `:851-863`, `:1371-1378`) and the tool pump (`ShellController.cpp:337-339`, which has no try), all end in `GUI_App::OnExceptionInMainLoop` → `generic_exception_handle` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:855-909`, `:9600-9604`).
  - Nothing in Agent/ or Home/ calls a reporting function.
- **What the code does:** OrcaSlicer's handler writes a log line and queues `wxLogError("OrcaSlicer got an unhandled exception: %1%")` with the exception text, then rethrows with `throw;`. The comment at `AgentHost.cpp:931-934` says this handler "logs it and reports it once". It does not report.
- **Rule broken:** "One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports."
- **What goes wrong:** Someone hits a bug, for example a page message missing a field, or Home asking for an unknown sign-in link (`OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:740`). They see an Orca-branded error that holds internal text such as "jusprin-agent-bridge: … ". Nothing reaches JusPrin. My inference, not run: because the handler rethrows, the app then quits.
- **Confidence:** high for the missing handler and report. Medium that the app quits.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 2. A model list whose shape changes crashes the app, because parsing throws on OrcaSlicer's HTTP thread
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:43-62`: `on_complete` calls `parse_model_list`.
  - `Agent/ModelCatalog.cpp:177-188`: it reads `response.at("data")`, `model.at("id").get<std::string>()`, `model.at("format")` and `model.at("credits").get<int>()`.
  - `src/slic3r/Utils/Http.cpp:796-801`: `perform()` runs `http_perform` on a `std::thread`. At `:519-526` that thread calls `completefn` directly, with no try around it.
- **What the code does:** If one model entry has no `format`, or its `credits` is not an integer, a `json` exception leaves a `std::thread` body. That calls `std::terminate`.
- **Rule broken:** "One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure…". The HTTP callback is an entry point with no handler. Keeping the parser strict is right; what is missing is the handler at the top.
- **What goes wrong:** One field changed on JusPrin Cloud, or in a provider's model list, makes the app quit each time it fetches models. That happens at launch and at sign-in. Nothing is reported.
- **Confidence:** high, by reading.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 3. An AI-request status the table does not name is shown as a network problem, and every 5xx as "temporarily unavailable"
- **Where:** `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:667-699` (`http_error`).
- **What the code does:** It sorts statuses by fixed rules and ends in `network_error`, "The AI request could not reach the … service.", with Retry. That last line catches:
  - 400, 404, 405, 409, 410 and 422;
  - 402 from any provider other than JusPrin's account;
  - any status other than 408 that came with no curl text.

  Any status of 500 or above other than 529 becomes `service_unavailable`. That includes JusPrin Cloud's own 502 `upstream_error` and 500 tracebacks. Because the `>= 500` test comes before the timeout test, the gateway's 504 `timeout` never becomes `timeout`. A 402 from JusPrin Cloud that is not `credits_exhausted` still becomes "You're out of credits." (`:683-685`). 401 and 403 always mean the sign-in ended or the key was rejected (`:673-674`, `:686-687`).
- **Rules broken:**
  - "A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause."
  - "Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it."
  - "When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected."
- **What goes wrong:**
  - JusPrin Cloud refuses the app's own request with 400 `invalid_request`, which is a bug on one of our two ends. The person is told to check their network and Retry, which never helps. Nobody hears of it.
  - Someone's OpenAI key cannot use the model they typed, and OpenAI answers 404. They get the same network sentence. Key setup takes the same path (`Agent/AgentSetup.cpp:112-127`).
  - A gateway fault reads as a provider outage.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 4. An error event inside the reply stream loses its code, so even causes the table names are shown as a generic failure
- **Where:** `Agent/ResponsesCodec.cpp:176-177` and `Agent/AnthropicCodec.cpp:404-405`. Both turn any `error` or `response.failed` event into `agent_service_error`, "The AI service could not complete the response.", and drop the event's code and message.
- **Related:** `Agent/AnthropicCodec.cpp:413-428`. `max_tokens` and `model_context_window_exceeded` become Incomplete. A stop reason this build does not know gets the invented sentence "ended its response for a reason this build does not know".
- **Rules broken:** "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own."
- **What goes wrong:** These failures, three of which have table entries, show as the same generic line with Retry:
  - Anthropic's mid-stream `overloaded_error` (table: `service_overloaded`);
  - the gateway's own mid-stream `timeout` (table: `timeout`);
  - the gateway's `upstream_error` (a gateway fault that should be reported).

  The saved message keeps only `agent_service_error`.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 5. Server: a reply that ends with the provider's own error event is recorded as completed, and its chat is kept as completed
- **Where:**
  - `gateway.py:301-307`: `self.outcome = 'completed'` is set whenever the upstream line iterator ends, whatever the last event was.
  - `stream.py:49-52` (Anthropic) and `:67-73` (Responses): an upstream `error` event, or a `response.error`, is rewritten to `STREAM_ERROR_MESSAGE` and forwarded, and the loop carries on.
  - `stream.py:100-109`: an unterminated last event is dropped without a word.
  - `gateway.py:241`: `keep()` then keeps the chat for fine-tuning as a completed reply.
  - `_log` (`gateway.py:330-361`) records outcome `completed` in Langfuse.
  - Nothing reports it.
- **Rules broken:** "Never record a failure as a success." "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own." (The sentence is "The model service failed while answering.")
- **What goes wrong:** When a provider fails mid-reply, the person sees a failure. The Langfuse record says completed. The kept chat, which is training data, holds a failed reply marked as complete. Nobody can count these failures.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 6. Server: upstream refusals are interpreted and given sentences of their own; only 401, 403 and 404 reach Sentry, and the provider's error text is dropped
- **Where:**
  - `upstream.py:197-208` (`error_for_status`): 400 and 422 become `invalid_request`, "The model service did not accept the request." Any other 4xx becomes `upstream_error` 502. Every status of 500 or above becomes `unavailable`.
  - `gateway.py:320-328` (`_upstream_failed`): Sentry is told only for `is_gateway_fault` statuses (401, 403 and 404, `upstream.py:211-214`). Everything else is `logger.warning`.
  - `gateway.py:312-315`: a transport error mid-stream sends an `upstream_error` event. It too is only a warning.
  - `gateway.py:321` drops the upstream body on purpose ("an upstream body can echo the prompt"). The client never receives the upstream status.
- **Rules broken:**
  - "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it."
  - "A log line is not a report: it reaches nobody."
  - "No other code reports." Sentry is called at the failure site, not in a top handler.
- **What goes wrong:** The provider starts refusing the gateway's requests with 400, for example after a model id or field changes. Every person's chat fails, and the app then calls it a network problem (finding 3). The server has only warning lines, with no provider text explaining why.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 7. Server: no endpoint has a top handler that reports and says "Something went wrong on our side"
- **Where:**
  - `gateway.py:136-185`: `_handle_in` catches only `GatewayError`. Anything else leaves `GatewayEndpoint.asgi` (`:117-130`) for daphne. That includes `ImproperlyConfigured` for a missing provider key (`upstream.py:185-187`), Redis or ledger errors in `admit` (`credits.py`), `remember_chat_title`, and an exception in `EventRewriter` mid-stream.
  - The Django views (`views.py`, `web.py`, `sign_in.py`) rely on Django's default 500.
  - `report_unexpected` does not exist at this commit.
- **Rule broken:** "One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side"…"
- **What goes wrong:**
  - Before the reply starts, the app gets daphne's plain-text 500. The app then shows "temporarily unavailable" (finding 3).
  - After the 200, the stream just stops.
  - Whether Sentry sees these depends on the Sentry SDK's logging integration catching daphne's error log line. I did not check that.
- **Confidence:** high for the missing handler. Unverified whether Sentry sees it.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 8. A project's chat state that fails to save is marked saved, and one that fails to read is overwritten with an empty one
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/ProjectPersistence.cpp:495-498`: `write_state_to` ignores `write_file`'s `false`.
  - `:400-401`: `flush` sets `m_dirty = false` anyway.
  - `:44-60`: `write_file` ignores `create_directories`' error code.
  - `:34-42`: `read_file` returns `{}` when the file cannot be opened, for any reason.
  - `:302-306`: `adopt_current_project` reads empty as "no state yet" and calls `start_fresh_identity`. That flushes a new document over the same `state.json` (in the non-managed case, `state_file_path()` and `write_state_to(jusprin_data_dir())` are the same file).
  - `:308-317`: a corrupt `state.json`, or one from a newer build, is renamed to `.corrupt`/`.newer` (the rename's error is ignored) and a fresh chat history starts. Nobody is told. The managed path (`:410-413`) throws `NewerFormatError` instead.
- **Rules broken:**
  - "Never record a failure as a success."
  - "A failure that arrives as a value … Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop."
  - "Do not … give it a default value."
  - "When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected."
- **What goes wrong:**
  - Someone's disk is full. Their chat looks fine, but none of it was saved, and the next open starts empty.
  - A transient read failure, such as a permissions change or a locked file, wipes the saved chats of a project opened from a folder.
  - None of this is reported.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 9. Attachments drop out of the request to the AI, or are sent empty, while the person sees them sent
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:1371-1378`: attachment ids that are unknown or not `staged` are "dropped rather than trusted". The ids come from our own page.
  - `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:3161-3178`: a text, G-code, SVG, image or PDF attachment whose file is missing or unreadable reads as an empty string (`ProjectPersistence::read_attachment_blob`, `ProjectPersistence.cpp:532-543`, returns `{}`). That empty content goes to the model. The same condition throws in `load_record_text` (`AgentHost.cpp:3023-3025`).
  - `Agent/ImageThumbnail.cpp:35-36`, `:49-50`: an image wx cannot decode, or cannot re-encode, returns nullopt. `AgentHost.cpp:3174-3178` then sends the original bytes.
- **Rules broken:** "Do not … give it a default value." "Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged." "When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected."
- **What goes wrong:** Someone attaches a photo of a failed print. The model answers as if there were no photo, or describes an empty file. Nobody is told.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 10. When the chat document cannot be saved, the person gets invented sentences, and two save results are ignored
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:2196-2213` (`checkpoint_active_chat`): the pin, the checkpoint save and the document save each return only a bool or optional, so the reason is gone.
  - `:2241-2245`: "The new chat could not be saved."
  - `:2331-2339`: "The current project could not be saved before restoration." and "JusPrin couldn't put the project back.", which then blocks the chat.
  - `:2342`: after a restore, the result of `checkpoint_active_chat()` is thrown away.
  - `:2237`: `save_chat_checkpoint`'s result for the new chat is ignored.
- **Rules broken:** "Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's … error text." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own." "Never record a failure as a success."
- **What goes wrong:** A failed save after a restore goes unnoticed, while the chat says "Restored this chat's saved project setup." Other save failures show a vague line, and nobody can learn why.
- **Confidence:** high.

# Error-handling sweep: trial findings

This file is the result of a reading-only sweep. It checks JusPrin's AI chat and Home code, and the JusPrin Cloud server's v2 code, against the trial copy of the error-handling rules and the `error-handling` audit skill. Nothing was built, run, changed or committed.

What was read:
- **Desktop app:** every `.cpp`/`.hpp` under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` and `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/` at commit `5e173c5e15`.
- **Server:** every `.py` under `web_ent/jusprin/v2/` except `tests/` and `migrations/`, at `2086b2ec64` in tsd-enterprise.

How it was judged:
- An outcome counts as decided by a person only if its cause is in `expected-errors-app.cpp` or `expected-errors-server.py`.
- Every other outcome counts as an unexpected error.

How to read the locations:
- Line numbers are from those two commits.
- App paths start at `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Server paths start at `web_ent/jusprin/v2/`.
- "Confirmed" means I read the code myself. Several findings were first reported by a reader subagent and then confirmed by me.
- Nothing was confirmed by running code.

## 1. Findings, most harmful first

### 1. In the desktop app, no failure is ever reported, and a thrown one reaches OrcaSlicer's generic handler
- **Where:**
  - The entry-point handler is `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:926-947` (`on_page_message`). It catches `json::exception`, adds the message type and id, and rethrows. That part is allowed.
  - The rethrow, and every other throw from the chat page, the timer pumps, Home's page messages (`Home/HomeHost.cpp:161`), Home's `CallAfter` bodies (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:749`, `:769-785`, `:851-863`, `:1371-1378`) and the tool pump (`ShellController.cpp:337-339`, which has no try), all end in `GUI_App::OnExceptionInMainLoop` → `generic_exception_handle` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:855-909`, `:9600-9604`).
  - Nothing in Agent/ or Home/ calls a reporting function.
- **What the code does:** OrcaSlicer's handler writes a log line and queues `wxLogError("OrcaSlicer got an unhandled exception: %1%")` with the exception text, then rethrows with `throw;`. The comment at `AgentHost.cpp:931-934` says this handler "logs it and reports it once". It does not report.
- **Rule broken:** "One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports."
- **What goes wrong:** Someone hits a bug, for example a page message missing a field, or Home asking for an unknown sign-in link (`OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:740`). They see an Orca-branded error that holds internal text such as "jusprin-agent-bridge: … ". Nothing reaches JusPrin. My inference, not run: because the handler rethrows, the app then quits.
- **Confidence:** high for the missing handler and report. Medium that the app quits.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 2. A model list whose shape changes crashes the app, because parsing throws on OrcaSlicer's HTTP thread
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:43-62`: `on_complete` calls `parse_model_list`.
  - `Agent/ModelCatalog.cpp:177-188`: it reads `response.at("data")`, `model.at("id").get<std::string>()`, `model.at("format")` and `model.at("credits").get<int>()`.
  - `src/slic3r/Utils/Http.cpp:796-801`: `perform()` runs `http_perform` on a `std::thread`. At `:519-526` that thread calls `completefn` directly, with no try around it.
- **What the code does:** If one model entry has no `format`, or its `credits` is not an integer, a `json` exception leaves a `std::thread` body. That calls `std::terminate`.
- **Rule broken:** "One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure…". The HTTP callback is an entry point with no handler. Keeping the parser strict is right; what is missing is the handler at the top.
- **What goes wrong:** One field changed on JusPrin Cloud, or in a provider's model list, makes the app quit each time it fetches models. That happens at launch and at sign-in. Nothing is reported.
- **Confidence:** high, by reading.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 3. An AI-request status the table does not name is shown as a network problem, and every 5xx as "temporarily unavailable"
- **Where:** `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:667-699` (`http_error`).
- **What the code does:** It sorts statuses by fixed rules and ends in `network_error`, "The AI request could not reach the … service.", with Retry. That last line catches:
  - 400, 404, 405, 409, 410 and 422;
  - 402 from any provider other than JusPrin's account;
  - any status other than 408 that came with no curl text.

  Any status of 500 or above other than 529 becomes `service_unavailable`. That includes JusPrin Cloud's own 502 `upstream_error` and 500 tracebacks. Because the `>= 500` test comes before the timeout test, the gateway's 504 `timeout` never becomes `timeout`. A 402 from JusPrin Cloud that is not `credits_exhausted` still becomes "You're out of credits." (`:683-685`). 401 and 403 always mean the sign-in ended or the key was rejected (`:673-674`, `:686-687`).

  - "A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause."
  - "Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it."
  - "When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected."
- **What goes wrong:**
  - JusPrin Cloud refuses the app's own request with 400 `invalid_request`, which is a bug on one of our two ends. The person is told to check their network and Retry, which never helps. Nobody hears of it.
  - Someone's OpenAI key cannot use the model they typed, and OpenAI answers 404. They get the same network sentence. Key setup takes the same path (`Agent/AgentSetup.cpp:112-127`).
  - A gateway fault reads as a provider outage.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 4. An error event inside the reply stream loses its code, so even causes the table names are shown as a generic failure
- **Where:** `Agent/ResponsesCodec.cpp:176-177` and `Agent/AnthropicCodec.cpp:404-405`. Both turn any `error` or `response.failed` event into `agent_service_error`, "The AI service could not complete the response.", and drop the event's code and message.

- **Rules broken:** "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own."
- **What goes wrong:** These failures, three of which have table entries, show as the same generic line with Retry:
  - Anthropic's mid-stream `overloaded_error` (table: `service_overloaded`);
  - the gateway's own mid-stream `timeout` (table: `timeout`);
  - the gateway's `upstream_error` (a gateway fault that should be reported).

  The saved message keeps only `agent_service_error`.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes (first reported by a reader).

### 5. Server: a reply that ends with the provider's own error event is recorded as completed, and its chat is kept as completed
- **Where:**
  - `gateway.py:301-307`: `self.outcome = 'completed'` is set whenever the upstream line iterator ends, whatever the last event was.
  - `stream.py:49-52` (Anthropic) and `:67-73` (Responses): an upstream `error` event, or a `response.error`, is rewritten to `STREAM_ERROR_MESSAGE` and forwarded, and the loop carries on.
  - `stream.py:100-109`: an unterminated last event is dropped without a word.
  - `gateway.py:241`: `keep()` then keeps the chat for fine-tuning as a completed reply.
  - `_log` (`gateway.py:330-361`) records outcome `completed` in Langfuse.
  - Nothing reports it.
- **Rules broken:** "Never record a failure as a success." "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text." "Do not … give it a sentence of its own." (The sentence is "The model service failed while answering.")
- **What goes wrong:** When a provider fails mid-reply, the person sees a failure. The Langfuse record says completed. The kept chat, which is training data, holds a failed reply marked as complete. Nobody can count these failures.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 6. Server: upstream refusals are interpreted and given sentences of their own; only 401, 403 and 404 reach Sentry, and the provider's error text is dropped
- **Where:**
  - `upstream.py:197-208` (`error_for_status`): 400 and 422 become `invalid_request`, "The model service did not accept the request." Any other 4xx becomes `upstream_error` 502. Every status of 500 or above becomes `unavailable`.
  - `gateway.py:320-328` (`_upstream_failed`): Sentry is told only for `is_gateway_fault` statuses (401, 403 and 404, `upstream.py:211-214`). Everything else is `logger.warning`.
  - `gateway.py:312-315`: a transport error mid-stream sends an `upstream_error` event. It too is only a warning.
  - `gateway.py:321` drops the upstream body on purpose ("an upstream body can echo the prompt"). The client never receives the upstream status.

  - "Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it."

  - `gateway.py:136-185`: `_handle_in` catches only `GatewayError`. Anything else leaves `GatewayEndpoint.asgi` (`:117-130`) for daphne. - **Where:** `gateway.py:243-247` (`_Turn.keep`): `except Exception: sentry_sdk.capture_exception(); logger.exception(...)`. The docstring calls it "the one error this gateway swallows".
- **Rules broken:** "Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it…" "No other code reports." Someone did decide this (the docstring), but it has no table entry.
- **What goes wrong:** The person is not affected. The fine-tuning record silently loses chats; Sentry does get them.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 26. Server: the stream record cannot tell a gateway crash from the app leaving
- **Where:** `gateway.py:300`: the outcome becomes `streaming` once the 200 is sent. If anything raises during the relay, `_log` in `relay`'s `finally` (`:231-235`) records `streaming`. That is the same outcome as the client going away, and the skill's production check reads it that way.
- **Rule broken:** "Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged." The record loses where the failure came from.
- **What goes wrong:** A gateway bug mid-reply looks like people pressing Stop.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 27. Server: broad catches are mapped onto expected answers
- **Where:**
  - `gateway.py:283-290`: `httpx.TimeoutException` becomes `timeout`. That includes `PoolTimeout`, which means the gateway's own pool was exhausted, not the provider being slow.
  - The same lines: `httpx.TransportError` becomes `unavailable`. That includes `LocalProtocolError`, `UnsupportedProtocol` and `ProxyError`, which are our own configuration or bugs.
  - `views.py:223`: `OSError` while checking a photo becomes `photo_unreadable`, even for a server I/O error.
  - `stream.py:24-27`: an upstream event that cannot be parsed is passed through unchanged.
  - `gateway.py:182`: `unquote(..., errors='replace')` on our own app's title header.
  - `views.py:92-98`: a webhook body that cannot be read gets a 400 with no report.
- **Rule broken:** "Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it…"
- **What goes wrong:** A gateway misconfiguration reads as a provider outage. A disk problem reads as the person's bad photo.
- **Confidence:** medium-high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 28. No occurrence of an expected error is counted, in either codebase
- **Where:**
  - Server: `gateway.py:410-415` (`_send_error`), `views.py:214-215` (`_refuse`) and `app_version.py:55-57` send expected answers with no count and no log line.
  - App: the `count_expected` in the trial's table file does not exist at this commit. Nothing in Agent/ or Home/ counts `credits_exhausted`, `rate_limited` or the others.
- **Rule broken:** "Each entry has a test, and each occurrence is counted."
- **What goes wrong:** How often people run out of credits or hit rate limits cannot be known from either side.
- **Confidence:** high.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 29. Our own stored JSON is read leniently: unknown values become defaults and fields that will not parse become `{}`
- **Where:**
  - `Agent/ProjectStateDocument.cpp:19-24`: an unknown role becomes Assistant.
  - `:37-47`: an unknown message state becomes Complete.
  - `:73-80`: an unknown action class becomes ReadOnly.
  - `:399-401`: `catch (const std::exception&) { session = 0; }`.
  - `:516-517`: `NLOHMANN_JSON_SERIALIZE_ENUM` reads an unknown chat-record item kind as the first value, User.
  - `:940-945`: `append_message` returns quietly when the chat does not exist. Neighbouring functions throw `logic_error` for the same kind of state.
  - `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:121-125`: `parsed_or_object` turns a tool result that will not parse into `{}`, which the model reads as a success with no data. It is used at about eight sites.
  - `Agent/RecordConversion.cpp:48-52`: the model's tool arguments that will not parse become `{}`. The comment there decides this.
- **Rules broken:** "Do not … give it a default value." "When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected." Some of these are deliberate compatibility rules (see part 3).
- **What goes wrong:** A record a newer build wrote could put a model's line into the chat as a person's message. A lost message vanishes without a word.
- **Confidence:** medium.
- **Confirmed:** yes.

### 30. Smaller confirmed points
- `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1212-1222` (`check_export`): every `error_code`, including permission denied, becomes "missing". Confidence high. Confirmed.
- `Home/PrinterWindow.cpp:145-153`: every web-view load error except a user cancel shows the window's "Nothing answered at %s…" problem, and the event's error code and text are dropped. That includes certificate and authentication failures, where something did answer. Confidence high. Confirmed.
- `Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:355-357` and `:910-914`: being unable to read the saved projects fails a call as `local_save_failed` with a fixed sentence. `EarlierLookup` keeps no reason. Confidence high. Confirmed.
- `Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:355-363` and `:424-431`: a picture the chat record could not keep makes `post()` return a bare false. The caller then says "The AI service could not start this request." (`AgentHost.cpp:2982-2983`), which blames the AI for a local disk failure. Confidence high. Confirmed.
- `Agent/AgentHost.cpp:3537-3541` (`set_agent`): a new AI service that arrives during a reply is dropped, after the page was already told "verified" or signed in. Rule: "If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering." Confidence medium. Confirmed.

Each item below names the reader's finding. I did not re-read the code for these, so treat them as leads:

- **Home, page fields:** missing fields from the Home page read as `""`, or `confirmed` read as "cancelled" (`HomeHost.cpp:204`, `:207` and on).

- **Silent no-ops in the host:** for example, a ToolCall event with no tool (`AgentHost.cpp:3410`).

- **Tool path checks:** `is_regular_file` errors are reworded as `invalid_arguments` (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:641-646`, `:899-904`).
- **Impossible tool states:** states that cannot happen get sentences instead of throws (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1280-1283`, `:2184-2186`, `:2283-2285`; `ToolRegistry.cpp:769`).
- **`setup_record`:** it guesses the refusal reason, and states a 120-character limit where 60 applies (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:2290-2293`).
- **Tool records left Running:** a throw inside `submit()` or `execute()` leaves the record Running, to be run again (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:622`).
- **Configuration states:** states that cannot happen become sentences (`ProviderFactory.cpp:145-172`, `AgentConfiguration.cpp:68-73`).
- **Port-in-use catch:** the catch for a port already in use takes every `boost::system::system_error` (`CloudSignInMachine.cpp:92-98`).

=== 6c776dc2b5 Include what the changed JusPrin files use
scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh against b3eed3bf4b named these: wx/timer.h beside
the timer bindings given a top handler, the Catch2 matcher headers beside
the new CHECK_THROWS_WITH tests, and the standard headers for std::move,
std::weak_ptr, std::function and the rest. OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.hpp now
declares ModelObject and wxCommandEvent, which it named without declaring.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M7JQFQ9A6PZ6WQDHN6461D2Y

=== fc1558eb09 Wait to delete the account while a printer or filament chat replies
Delete account in Preferences waited only for a reply in the project chat.
A reply running in a printer or filament chat went on holding the account's
sign-in after the server had deleted the account. The shell now tells the
Preferences window whether a reply runs in either chat.

The shell harness's --delete-account-waits runs it against a stand-in
server: during a printer chat's reply nothing is deleted, and once the reply
ends the deletion goes through. Before the fix the server got the deletion
during the reply.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M7JQ1K8J2J2JMAME1QAXV9K0

=== a31c8def54 Shell harness: a chat checkpoint and an attachment write now throw when they fail
The unavailable-storage scenario expects the checkpoint to stop with the
autosave's own error, and the blank-project scenario no longer reads a
result from the attachment write.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M7JQ1DTCVYVQRC64BV2NT6AS

=== 0c351ee300 Let the app's own failures in chats, attachments and saves go up
A chat checkpoint, chat switch, restoration or new chat whose project save
fails now throws the autosave's own error instead of showing a sentence
made up for it. A checkpoint asked for while a reply, tool or queued
message runs still waits for a later call.

Attachment blobs that cannot be written or read, attachment folders that
cannot be removed, a chat-titles file that cannot be read or written, and
a chat state in an opened project that cannot be read now throw with the
file system's error. A message naming an attachment the host does not
hold as staged, and a request whose attachment file is gone, stop instead
of being sent without it.

The provider agent throws when the HTTP transport refuses to start a
request, and when a picture the chat record cannot keep fails to write.
A stored tool call's session or tool result that will not read, and a
message for a chat the document does not hold, are errors, not defaults.

A tool call that fails in the app's own work still goes to the AI model,
and is now also reported when automatic reports are on, with no dialog.
The MCP config file's refusals are their own exception types, so the
preview and connect handlers catch only those and no longer match text.
Project-state subscribers JusPrin adds run under a top handler, because a
throw from a transaction's destructor would otherwise end the app.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M7JNZK2ZFTYZ3BXRWMZFYRMH

=== 625253a973 Report a key or sign-in the settings file could not keep as unexpected
A verified key or a JusPrin sign-in that could not be written to the
settings file was shown as working, with a warning that it would be gone
after a restart ("This key could not be saved, so it will have to be
entered again next time JusPrin starts.", and the same for a sign-in). A
settings file that cannot be written is nothing the person can act on.

Saving now throws when AppConfig::save() leaves the settings unsaved. The
key check's top handler, and a new one around the sign-in in
AgentHost::pump_setup, report it and end in "Something went wrong on our
side"; on Home the timer's handler reports it. A sign-in is over before
its account is stored, so a failed store leaves it idle instead of
checking again.

The warning, its "works until restart" key row on the page and the
CloudSignInOutcome::saved flag are gone.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M7JM64BARH41326ZQS4N7SYZ

=== b840de45b7 Give every entry point JusPrin's own code starts a top handler
A CallAfter body, a timer, an HTTP callback or a thread that JusPrin
starts had no handler at its top. An exception from a CallAfter or timer
reached OrcaSlicer's generic handler, which ends the main loop; one from
an HTTP callback or a thread called std::terminate. A model list with an
entry missing its "id" made the app abort at launch (reproduced: exit
134, "terminating due to uncaught exception of type
nlohmann::detail::out_of_range: key 'id' not found").

reported(doing, body), in Support/ErrorReport.hpp, wraps such a body: an
exception that leaves it goes to report_unexpected_error, which the person
sees as "Something went wrong on our side". report_unexpected_error now
moves itself to the main thread when called from another. The MCP
server's thread, which the GUI-free tests also build, reports through a
handler AgentHost gives it. The file picker's own try is gone: the
CallAfter's handler covers it.

Kenneth decided an exception leaving any other native event stays
OrcaSlicer's, as upstream handles it; GUI_App::OnExceptionInMainLoop is
unchanged.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M7JKX5JQE97BN5AS9X6M59EY

=== 8bbe48c4b2 Report a reply the AI service cut short or sent unreadable as unexpected
The reply decoders and the request loop gave failures a person cannot act
on sentences of their own: "The AI service stopped before finishing its
response.", "The AI service ended before a complete response arrived.",
"The AI service returned an unreadable streaming response.", "The AI
service kept pausing its response.", "AI returned an invalid tool call."
and three more. Each now stops the turn as unexpected: the loop throws
UnexpectedServiceAnswer with what the service sent, the agent pump's
handler reports it, and the chat shows "Something went wrong on our side"
with Retry.

StreamEvent::Kind::Incomplete is gone: a response cut short by its token
limit or context window is a ServiceError like any other.

The model declining to answer (stop reason "refusal") keeps its sentence:
it is the model's answer, not a failure, and is left for Kenneth to decide.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M7JKC7A6ZCQ6K3P0Z18BSYRF

=== 20d71dcac6 Report AI request failures a person cannot act on as unexpected
An AI request that fails now tells the person the cause only where they
can do something about it. On a JusPrin account, by the gateway's error
code: signed out, out of credits, app too old, request too large, too
many requests. With their own key, by the HTTP status alone: 401 (key
rejected), 413 (too large), 429 (rate limited). A request that got no
answer at all says the service could not be reached.

Every other answer, and every error the service sends inside a reply,
throws UnexpectedServiceAnswer with the service's status, request id and
body. The handler at the top of the agent's stream and setup pumps
reports it through report_unexpected_error and the chat shows "Something
went wrong on our side" with Retry.

Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing
about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to
report a problem." The separate sentences for an overloaded, unavailable
or timed-out service are deleted.

The HTTP transport now reads the request-id / x-request-id header so the
report carries it.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M7JK5T8YSGBKQJQMZPJD3P03

//   hidden, at a cost beyond one more tool call.
//
// So a refusal carries the reason the app read from the event (a plug-in's

namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::Agent::ToolErrors {

inline constexpr std::string_view kCodes[] = {
    // Fix the arguments and call again.
    "invalid_arguments",
    "unknown_tool",
    "unknown_skill",
    // Not run because an earlier call of the same response failed; decide again.
    "not_run",
    // Read the state again, then call again.
    "not_found",       // an id that is not in the open project
    "stale_workspace", // the project changed since the read the call was based on
    "feature_expired", // a face, edge or hole handle from an earlier revision
    "connection_lost", // MCP bridge only: the outcome is unknown
    // Wait, then call again.
    "busy",
    // Do the step the message names first, with another tool.
    "needs_step",
    // Ask the person: the decision or the action is theirs.
    "opened_before",
    "workspace_unavailable", // no open project, or no FFF printer selected
    // Stop and tell the person.
    "refused",           // OrcaSlicer does not do this here
    "failed",            // OrcaSlicer tried and failed
    "local_save_failed", // the project could not be saved
    "cancelled",

    // The settings tools' corrections (tool guide, "Error codes").
    "unknown_setting",
    "unsupported_scope",
    "invalid_setting_value",
    "incompatible_settings",
    "unsupported_setting_mutation",
    "withheld_setting",
    "unknown_preset",
    "incompatible_preset",
    "unsupported_plate",
    "not_selected",
    "read_only_preset",
    "name_taken",
    "invalid_preset_name",
    "not_in_project",

    // The printer and filament chats' own refusals.
    "unknown_nozzle",
    "not_in_this_conversation",
    "no_printer",
    "other_printer",
    "stock_profile",
    "unknown_printer",
    "connection_unavailable",
    "unknown_device",
    "address_needed",
    "too_many",
    "already_added",
    "add_failed",
    "change_failed",
    "nothing_to_change",
    "not_saved",

    // The internal record tools, which only the page calls.
    "slice_required",
    "missing_plate",
    "missing_build",
    "invalid_progress",
};

inline bool registered(std::string_view code)
{
    return std::find(std::begin(kCodes), std::end(kCodes), code) != std::end(kCodes);
}

} // namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin::Agent::ToolErrors

"""The gateway's own error answers, and the expected-errors table.

Every error the gateway returns has the body
{"type": "error", "error": {"code": <code>, "message": <message>}}, never bytes
from upstream. The client treats 401 as "signed out", so 401 means only that
the person's own token was missing or rejected. credits_exhausted adds what the
client needs to offer a way on, beside "error"; update_required adds
minimumVersion, the oldest release still served.

An error is expected only when a person decided what the product does for that
named cause; EXPECTED holds those decisions. Every other failure is unexpected:
nothing handles it where it happens, the one handler at the top of the endpoint
reports it, and the app is told UNEXPECTED_CODE with UNEXPECTED_MESSAGE.
"""
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Expected:
    message: str    # what the person is told
    cause: str
    next_step: str  # what they can do next


# Kenneth confirmed these entries on 2026-11-15: "This table looks good. Confirmed."
# The causes and next steps are in the words he confirmed. On 2026-11-16 he had
# the entries for a provider or the server being slow, busy, overloaded or down
# taken out: "if the error is something that user can do nothing about, just
# show the user a generic error message and give user a way to report a problem."
EXPECTED = {
    'unauthorized': Expected(
        'Sign in to JusPrin to continue.',
        cause='Signed out', next_step='Sign in again'),
    # The sentence names both numbers; credits_exhausted() fills them in.
    'credits_exhausted': Expected(
        'This message needs {cost} {unit}; you have {balance}.',
        cause='Out of credits', next_step='Get more credits'),
    'update_required': Expected(
        'This version of JusPrin can no longer connect to JusPrin accounts. Get the new version to keep using your account.',
        cause='App too old', next_step='Get the new version'),
    'rate_limited': Expected(
        'Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.',
        cause='Too many turns a minute', next_step='Wait and retry'),
    'request_too_large': Expected(
        'The request is too large.',
        cause='Chat or report photos too large', next_step='New chat, or fewer pictures'),
    'text_too_short': Expected(
        'A report needs a few sentences.',
        cause='Print report too short', next_step='Write more'),
    'photo_needed': Expected(
        'A report needs a photo of the printed object.',
        cause='Print report has no photo', next_step='Add a photo'),
    'photo_unreadable': Expected(
        'That photo could not be read.',
        cause='Report photo cannot be opened', next_step='Add a different photo'),
    'already_reported': Expected(
        'This print already has a report.',
        cause='Print already reported', next_step='Nothing'),
}

UNEXPECTED_CODE = 'server_error'
UNEXPECTED_MESSAGE = 'Something went wrong on our side'

# Refusals of a request the app itself sent. Kenneth, 2026-11-15, on these
# three: "Treat them as unexpected errors." They are still answered as
# refusals here, with these words.
REFUSALS = {
    'invalid_request': 'The request is not valid.',
    'unknown_model': 'This model is not available.',
    'method_not_allowed': 'This method is not allowed here.',
}

MESSAGES = {**{code: entry.message for code, entry in EXPECTED.items()}, **REFUSALS,
            UNEXPECTED_CODE: UNEXPECTED_MESSAGE}


class GatewayError(Exception):
    """An answer the gateway gives instead of forwarding. Raised inside one
    request and turned into a response at the endpoint boundary only."""

- Provider overloaded → "The AI service is overloaded." → Wait, then Retry
- Provider down or unreachable from our server → "The AI service is temporarily unavailable." → Retry
- Provider too slow, or connection stalled → "The AI request timed out." → Retry
- No network → "The AI request could not reach the service." → Check the network, then Retry

**Server, expected answers:**
- Signed out → "Sign in to JusPrin to continue." → Sign in again
- Out of credits → "This message needs N credits; you have M." → Get more credits (the table first shown to him said "You do not have enough credits for this message.", which the server never sent; asked which to keep on 2026-11-15, he took the pick, what the server sends: "Go with your picks for both")
- App too old → "This version of JusPrin can no longer connect to JusPrin accounts. Get the new version to keep using your account." → Get the new version
- Too many turns a minute, or provider limiting us → "Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again." → Wait and retry
- Server's slots for large requests all taken → "JusPrin is busy right now. Try again in a moment." → Retry
- Provider down, overloaded or unreachable → "The model service is unavailable. Try again shortly." → Retry
- Provider too slow → "The model service took too long to answer." → Retry
- Chat or report photos too large → "The request is too large." → New chat, or fewer pictures
- Print report too short → "A report needs a few sentences." → Write more
- Print report has no photo → "A report needs a photo of the printed object." → Add a photo
- Report photo cannot be opened → "That photo could not be read." → Add a different photo
- Print already reported → "This print already has a report." → Nothing

Also confirmed by the same answer: a provider's own "overloaded" event partway through a reply (Anthropic `overloaded_error`, OpenAI `server_is_overloaded`) counts as the "unavailable" entry and is not reported. The server table is in code since 2026-11-15: `web_ent/jusprin/v2/errors.py` `EXPECTED` (commits 057ea6d412, then the credits correction).

The second column is as shown to him: the app column is the build session's description of the sentence, not always the literal on-screen string, so check each against the code when rebuilding. The server's four other answers (invalid_request, unknown_model, method_not_allowed, upstream_error) stay unexpected: "Agreed. Treat them as unexpected errors."
